decisive_checks: For H=(Z/2)^2 and omega0(u,v)=(-1)^(u1*v2), the base cocycle identity follows by bilinearity. A pure shift x and identity-coordinate vectors y,z produce literal four values (1,1,1,-1); the two sides disagree. The genuine free-group action moves the identity coordinate.
The same pure-shift argument forces omega0(a,b)=1 for every base pair if the unshifted full-product expression is a cocycle. This covers alternative base groups and representatives.

Pauli matrices Z^u2 X^u1 give a trace-preserving L_omega0(H)=M2(C), an allowed nontrivial amenable tracial base. Tensor Pauli unitaries and shift implementers construct the theorem left side using the corrected cocycle. The literal right side would require an untwisted group algebra equal to M2(C); L2 dimension forces group order four, whose group algebra is commutative.
